brief.subject: IRS lets tax pros pay for business clients online
brief.headline: IRS Tax Pro Account Now Handles Business Client Payments
brief.dek: Tax pros can now pay for business clients online, the IRS fixes its opportunity zone reporting proposal, and California voters reject a wealth tax.
brief.lede: Tax professionals can now make certain payments for their business clients through the IRS Tax Pro Account. The IRS announced the change on Nov. 6.

sections.heading: Tax Pro Account Adds Business Payments
bullets: Tax Pro Account now supports certain payments made on behalf of business clients.
Bookkeepers and preparers may be able to handle some client payments without separate client logins.
The IRS announced the expansion on Nov. 6.

sections.heading: Opportunity Zone Reporting Rules Corrected
bullets: The IRS published corrections to proposed rule REG-116506-25, first released on September 11, 2026.
The proposal would require qualified opportunity funds to file information returns and give statements to investors who dispose of investments.
Qualified opportunity zone businesses would also have to give statements to the funds that hold interests in them.

sections.heading: California Voters Reject Billionaire Tax
bullets: About 52.9% of voters rejected the one-time, 5% wealth tax in preliminary results Monday evening.
Support came in at 47.1%, so the measure appears headed for defeat.
Business owners watching California tax policy can expect no new one-time wealth levy for now.

sections.heading: Trump Account Investment Rules Advance
bullets: The IRS issued a hearing notice on its proposed rules for eligible Trump account investments.
Those proposed rules were first published on August 21, 2026.
The rules limit which assets the accounts can hold before the calendar year the beneficiary turns 18.

items.snippet: In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, the IRS is inviting comments on the information collection request outlined in this notice.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.

items.title: IRS Expands Tax Pro Account to Allow Business Client Payments
items.snippet: Tax professionals can now make certain payments on behalf of their business clients through Tax Pro Account, the IRS announced on Nov. 6.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance on Eligible Investments for Trump Accounts; Hearing
items.snippet: This document provides a notice of proposed rulemaking (CC- 00349938-26) published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026. The proposed regulations provided guidance regarding eligible investments, which are the only assets in which the Trump account may be invested before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains 18.
